mcqs.question: Which statement best distinguishes a physical change from a chemical change?

options.A: In a physical change the chemical composition of the substance remains unchanged, whereas in a chemical change new substances are formed.
options.B: A physical change always involves a change of state, while a chemical change never does.
options.C: Chemical changes can be easily reversed, but physical changes cannot.
options.D: Physical changes always release energy, whereas chemical changes always absorb energy.

mcqs.answer: In a physical change the chemical composition of the substance remains unchanged, whereas in a chemical change new substances are formed.
mcqs.explanation: A physical change only alters the form or state of a substance; its molecules remain the same. A chemical change involves breaking and forming of bonds, producing substances with different chemical formulas. Options B, C and D describe incorrect generalizations.

mcqs.learning_point: Classify matter into elements, compounds and mixtures
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a pure element?
mcqs.explanation: An element consists of only one type of atom. Oxygen gas contains only O atoms, making it a pure element. Air is a mixture of gases, water is a compound of hydrogen and oxygen, and sodium chloride is a compound of sodium and chlorine.

mcqs.question: A mixture of sand and iron filings and a sugar solution in water are observed. Which description is correct?

options.C: The sand‑iron mixture is heterogeneous, while the sugar solution is homogeneous.
options.D: The sand‑iron mixture is homogeneous, while the sugar solution is heterogeneous.

mcqs.answer: The sand‑iron mixture is heterogeneous, while the sugar solution is homogeneous.
mcqs.explanation: In a heterogeneous mixture the components are visibly distinct (sand and iron filings). In a homogeneous mixture the composition is uniform throughout, as in a true solution of sugar in water. Options A, B and D misclassify the mixtures.

mcqs.question: A student claims that a beam of light is matter because it can be detected. Which of the following statements correctly defines matter?

options.A: Matter is anything that has mass and occupies space.
options.B: Matter is anything that can be seen with the naked eye.
options.C: Matter is only the solid substances around us.
options.D: Matter is any form of energy, including light.

mcqs.answer: Matter is anything that has mass and occupies space.
mcqs.explanation: The scientific definition of matter requires both mass and volume (space occupation). Light has energy but no rest mass and does not occupy space in the same sense, so it is not matter. Options B, C and D are incorrect or incomplete definitions.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements reflects a common misconception about physical and chemical properties?

options.A: Melting point is a physical property.
options.B: Reactivity with acid is a chemical property.
options.D: Boiling point is a physical property.

mcqs.explanation: Density depends only on mass and volume, which are physical attributes; therefore it is a physical property. Options A, B and D correctly associate the properties with their categories, while option C mistakenly labels a physical property as chemical.

mcqs.question: When a piece of magnesium ribbon is heated in air and turns white, which statement correctly explains the observed change?

options.A: The white substance formed is MgO, indicating a chemical change.
options.B: The ribbon only melted, which is a physical change.
options.C: The colour change is due solely to temperature, so it is a physical change.
options.D: No new substance is formed; therefore the process is purely physical.

mcqs.answer: The white substance formed is MgO, indicating a chemical change.
mcqs.explanation: Heating magnesium in air leads to oxidation, producing magnesium oxide (MgO), a new chemical substance—hence a chemical change. Options B, C and D ignore the formation of a new compound.

mcqs.learning_point: Classify matter into elements, compounds and mixtures
mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly matches each substance with its category?

options.A: (i) O₂ – element, (ii) H₂O – compound, (iii) Air – mixture
options.B: (i) O₂ – compound, (ii) H₂O – element, (iii) Air – mixture
options.C: (i) O₂ – element, (ii) H₂O – mixture, (iii) Air – compound
options.D: (i) O₂ – mixture, (ii) H₂O – element, (iii) Air – compound

mcqs.answer: (i) O₂ – element, (ii) H₂O – compound, (iii) Air – mixture
mcqs.explanation: O₂ consists of only oxygen atoms, making it an element. H₂O contains hydrogen and oxygen atoms chemically combined, so it is a compound. Air is a physical mixture of several gases. Options B, C and D misclassify one or more substances.

mcqs.question: In a competitive‑exam question, the student is asked to identify a homogeneous mixture and a heterogeneous mixture respectively. Which pair is correct?
mcqs.explanation: A salt solution is uniform throughout, qualifying as a homogeneous mixture. Granite consists of visibly distinct minerals, making it heterogeneous. In options A, B, and C the classifications are deliberately reversed or inaccurate according to NCERT definitions.
